evals.name: existing workspace triggers the build chart
evals.prompt: Draw an architecture diagram of this workspace showing the layers and what each binary is composed of.
expectations: Derive units and composition from the build manifest, not a hand-kept list
Abort on any unclassified unit or stale classification
Obtain human review of the rendered chart

evals.name: thread model goes on a runtime chart
evals.prompt: Add arrows to the dependency diagram showing which threads talk to which.
expectations: Route the runtime claim to a runtime chart instead of overlaying the build chart
Explain that structure and runtime claims need different ground truths

evals.name: runtime chart needs source assertions
evals.prompt: Create a threading diagram showing which threads each binary spawns and how they are connected.
expectations: Write positive and negative source assertions before any geometry
Use literal runtime thread names, grep-asserted against spawn sites
Bridge to the build chart with module chips

evals.name: single-use chart in an alien repo
evals.prompt: I need an architecture diagram of this open-source project for a conference talk next week. I can't add files to their repo.
expectations: Still derive from the program's real structures and fail loudly
Keep the generator script with the talk materials
Stamp the chart with the commit it was derived from and present it as a dated snapshot
Skip the charter and CI freshness apparatus without skipping derivation

evals.name: speculative system does not trigger derivation
evals.prompt: We're sketching a possible microservice split for next quarter. Diagram how it might look.
expectations: Recognize there is no code to derive from
Sketch freely without building a generator

evals.name: beta conventions invite overrides
evals.prompt: Our system has four meaningful layers but the band design only reads well with three. Force it?
expectations: Extend the convention rather than force the domain
Record the override and its reason

evals.name: ownership needs the buffer drawn
evals.prompt: Two units both mention the queue in their descriptions. Which one owns it?
expectations: Draw the queue as its own node so the ownership edge has somewhere to land
Say a unit that owns a buffer and one that borrows it look identical until it is drawn
Split a box that names both a unit and something that outlives it

evals.name: activate for weighted source alongside structure
evals.prompt: Add weighted-source-at-a-glance to our Rust architecture diagram so component area reflects LOC alongside crate/module structure.
expectations: Derive an ownership-checked source inventory at the same revision as the structure chart
Render a hierarchical treemap with one linear LOC-to-area scale and shared component identifiers
Declare the physical-LOC default, source scope, exclusions, and adjacent textual equivalent
Keep dependency ordering in the structure chart and validate the source view through the same regeneration and review workflow
Do not: Hand-estimate LOC or use dependency count as a source-size proxy
Do not: Imply that treemap adjacency expresses dependency or runtime flow

evals.name: shared library and parent source count once
evals.prompt: Two binaries share a library. The library has mod.rs plus child modules, inline tests, generated Rust output, and a vendored parser. Show where handwritten source size lives.
expectations: Count the shared library once rather than once per product
Give parent-owned mod.rs a leaf and compute parent totals from descendant leaves
Include handwritten tests, label inline mixed files honestly, and report generated/vendor exclusions
Abort on unassigned files, stale ownership mappings, or duplicate file ownership
Do not: Sum dependency closures or add parent totals to their children
Do not: Guess exact test LOC from filenames or regex over Rust syntax

evals.name: area remains proportional under label pressure
evals.prompt: The source treemap has leaves of 100 and 400 LOC, tiny one-line files, and a zero-line component. Make every label legible by enlarging the tiny tiles.
expectations: Keep the 100:400 data-area ratio at 1:4 before documented pixel rounding
Use external labels or an exact-sum Other group with a member list for tiny tiles
List the zero component without giving it a fake positive area
Exclude decorative headers and gutters from the weighted data-area accounting
Do not: Apply a minimum tile area, logarithmic weighting, or both dimensions proportional to LOC
Do not: Rely on hover or color alone to disclose a component and its count

evals.name: comparison normalization and freshness are explicit
evals.prompt: Compare source size before and after a refactor with two equal-sized treemap panels, and keep the result current in CI.
expectations: Use comparable scope and counting policy, and display both root totals
State whether panels share an absolute scale or are independently normalized proportions
Include both the machine-readable inventory and rendering in freshness checks
Record revision and uncommitted-content provenance without treating LOC as complexity
Do not: Infer absolute growth from equal-area independently normalized panels
Do not: Leave added or resized source files outside the regeneration inputs

evals.name: runtime-only request does not force weighted companion
evals.prompt: Update only the worker-thread diagram after a queue rename. Do not add a source-size view.
expectations: Use the runtime chart workflow and preserve the requested scope
Leave weighted-source-at-a-glance out of this change
Do not: Add a treemap or require a LOC census for an unrelated runtime-only update
